title: 第一章 故事中的权力

outline.title: 理论化歧义与追踪权力

en: This is a story within a story—so slippery at the edges that one wonders when and where it started and whether it will ever end. By the middle of February 1836, the army of general Antonio López de Santa Anna had reached the crumbling walls of the old mission of San Antonio de Valero in the Mexican province of Tejas. Few traces of the Franciscan priests who had built the mission more than a century before had survived the combined assaults of time and of a succession of less religious residents. Intermittent squatters, Spanish and Mexican soldiers, had turned the place into something of a fort and nicknamed it "the Alamo," from the name of a Spanish cavalry unit that undertook one of the many transformations of the crude compound. Now, three years after Santa Anna first gained power in independent Mexico, a few English-speaking squatters occupied the place, refusing to surrender to his superior force. Luckily for Santa Anna, the squatters were outnumbered—at most 189 potential fighters—and the structure itself was weak. The conquest would be easy, or so thought Santa Anna.
zh: 这是一个故事中的故事——边缘如此滑溜，让人疑惑它始于何时何地、又是否会终结。1836年2月中旬，安东尼奥·洛佩斯·德·圣安纳将军的军队已抵达墨西哥特哈斯省圣安东尼奥·德·巴莱罗老传教站坍塌的墙垣。一个多世纪前修建这座传教站的方济各会神父几乎没有留下什么痕迹，岁月与一茬茬不那么虔诚的居住者的轮番冲击抹去了它们。先后在此擅自驻扎的西班牙和墨西哥士兵把这地方改造成了一座准要塞，并给它起了个绰号“阿拉莫”。这个名字来自一支西班牙骑兵部队，是它对这座简陋院落作了历次改造中的一次。如今，距圣安纳首次在独立后的墨西哥掌权已过三年，几个说英语的占地者占据着这里，拒绝向他的优势兵力投降。对圣安纳来说幸运的是，占地者人数处于劣势——最多189名可能的战斗人员——而且建筑本身并不坚固。征服会很容易，圣安纳这么想。

en: The conquest was not easy: the siege persisted through twelve days of cannonade. On March 6, Santa Anna blew the horns that Mexicans traditionally used to announce an attack to the death. Later on that same day, his forces finally broke through the fort, killing most of the defenders. But a few weeks later, on April 21, at San Jacinto, Santa Anna fell prisoner to Sam Houston, the freshly certified leader of the secessionist Republic of Texas.
zh: 征服并不容易：围攻持续了十二天的炮击。3月6日，圣安纳吹响了墨西哥人传统上用来宣告决死进攻的号角。当天晚些时候，他的部队终于攻破要塞，杀死了大部分守军。但几周后的4月21日，在圣哈辛托，圣安纳却成了萨姆·休斯顿的俘虏——这位刚刚获承认的得克萨斯共和国领袖，这个共和国已宣布脱离墨西哥。

en: Santa Anna recovered from that upset; he went on to be four more times the leader of a much reduced Mexico. But in important ways, he was doubly defeated at San Jacinto. He lost the battle of the day, but he also lost the battle he had won at the Alamo. Houston's men had punctuated their victorious attack on the Mexican army with repeated shouts of "Remember the Alamo! Remember the Alamo!" With that reference to the old mission, they doubly made history. As actors, they captured Santa Anna and neutralized his forces. As narrators, they gave the Alamo story a new meaning. The military loss of March was no longer the end point of the narrative but a necessary turn in the plot, the trial of the heroes, which, in turn, made final victory both inevitable and grandiose. With the battle cry of San Jacinto, Houston's men reversed for more than a century the victory Santa Anna thought he had gained in San Antonio.
zh: 圣安纳从那场挫败中恢复过来；此后他又四次领导那个版图大为缩水的墨西哥。但在重要的意义上，他在圣哈辛托遭受了双重失败。他输掉了当天的战斗，也输掉了他在阿拉莫已经赢得的那场战斗。休斯顿的人在反复高呼“铭记阿拉莫！铭记阿拉莫！”的呐喊中，向墨西哥军队发起胜利的进攻。借着对那座老传教站的指涉，他们双重地创造了历史。作为行动者，他们俘获了圣安纳，瓦解了他的军队。作为叙述者，他们赋予阿拉莫故事新的意义。三月那场军事失败不再是叙述的终点，而成了情节中必要的转折、英雄受的试炼，反过来使最后的胜利既不可避免又辉煌壮丽。随着圣哈辛托的战斗口号，休斯顿的人在一个多世纪里颠倒了圣安纳自以为在圣安东尼奥赢得的胜利。

en: Human beings participate in history both as actors and as narrators. The inherent ambivalence of the word "history" in many modern languages, including English, suggests this dual participation. In vernacular use, history means both the facts of the matter and a narrative of those facts, both "what happened" and "that which is said to have happened." The first meaning places the emphasis on the sociohistorical process, the second on our knowledge of that process or on a story about that process.
zh: 人类既作为行动者、也作为叙述者参与历史。“历史”一词在许多现代语言（包括英语）中固有的歧义，暗示了这种双重参与。在日常用法中，历史既指事情本身，也指关于这些事情的叙述，既指“发生了什么”，也指“据说发生了什么”。第一种含义把重心放在社会历史过程上，第二种放在我们对那个过程的知识上，或放在关于那个过程的故事上。

en: If I write "The history of the United States begins with the Mayflower," a statement many readers may find simplistic and controversial, there will be little doubt that I am suggesting that the first significant event in the process that eventuated in what we now call the United States is the landing of the Mayflower. Consider now a sentence grammatically identical to the preceding one and perhaps as controversial: "The history of France starts with Michelet." The meaning of the word "history" has unambiguously shifted from the sociohistorical process to our knowledge of that process. The sentence affirms that the first significant narrative about France was the one written by Jules Michelet.
zh: 如果我写“美国的历史始于五月花号”——许多读者可能觉得这个说法简单化且有争议——那么几乎可以肯定，我是在暗示：在最终演变为今天所谓美国的那个过程中，第一个有意义的事件是五月花号的登陆。现在考虑一个语法上与前句完全相同、也许同样有争议的句子：“法国的历史始于米什莱。”“历史”一词的含义已明确无误地从社会历史过程转向我们对那个过程的知识。这个句子断定：关于法国的第一个重要叙述，是儒勒·米什莱写的那一个。

en: Yet the distinction between what happened and that which is said to have happened is not always clear. Consider a third sentence: "The history of the United States is a history of migration." The reader may choose to understand both uses of the word history as emphasizing the sociohistorical process. Then, the sentence seems to suggest that the fact of migration is the central element in the evolution of the United States. But an equally valid interpretation of that sentence is that the best narrative about the United States is a story of migrations. That interpretation becomes privileged if I add a few qualifiers: "The true history of the United States is a history of migrations. That history remains to be written."
zh: 然而，“发生了什么”与“据说发生了什么”之间的区分并不总是清楚。考虑第三个句子：“美国的历史是一部移民史。”读者可以把两处“历史”都理解为强调社会历史过程。那么，这个句子似乎在暗示：移民这一事实是美国演进中的核心要素。但同样成立的解释是：关于美国的最佳叙述是一部移民的故事。如果我加上几个限定语，后一种解释就占了上风：“真正的美国历史是一部移民史。那部历史尚待书写。”

en: Yet a third interpretation may place the emphasis on the sociohistorical process for the first use of the word "history" and on knowledge and narrative for its second use in the same sentence, thus suggesting that the best narrative about the United States is one of which migration is the central theme. This third interpretation is possible only because we implicitly acknowledge an overlap between the sociohistorical process and our knowledge of it, an overlap significant enough to allow us to suggest, with varying degree of metaphorical intent, that the history of the United States is a story of migrations. Not only can history mean either the sociohistorical process or our knowledge of that process, but the boundary between the two meanings is often quite fluid.
zh: 还有第三种解释：同一句中第一个“历史”强调社会历史过程，第二个强调知识与叙述，从而暗示关于美国的最佳叙述是以移民为中心主题的那一种。这第三种解释之所以可能，只是因为我们默认社会历史过程与我们对它的知识之间存在重叠，而且这重叠足够大，让我们可以带着不同程度的隐喻意图说，美国的历史是一部移民的故事。历史不仅可以指社会历史过程或我们对那个过程的知识，而且两种含义之间的边界常常相当流动。

en: The vernacular use of the word history thus offers us a semantic ambiguity: an irreducible distinction and yet an equally irreducible overlap between what happened and that which is said to have happened. Yet it suggests also the importance of context: the overlap and the distance between the two sides of historicity may not be susceptible to a general formula. The ways in which what happened and that which is said to have happened are and are not the same may itself be historical.
zh: 于是，“历史”一词的日常用法给了我们一种语义歧义：在“发生了什么”与“据说发生了什么”之间，既有不可化约的区分，又有同样不可化约的重叠。但它也暗示了语境的重要：历史性两面之间的重叠与距离，未必能套用一个通用公式。“发生了什么”与“据说发生了什么”在何种方式上相同又在何种方式上不同，这本身可能就是历史性的。

en: Words are not concepts and concepts are not words: between the two are the layers of theory accumulated throughout the ages. But theories are built on words and with words. Thus it is not surprising that the ambiguity offered by the vernacular use of the word history has caught the attention of many thinkers since at least antiquity. What is surprising is the reluctance with which theories of history have dealt with this fundamental ambiguity. Indeed, as history became a distinguishable profession, theorists have followed two incompatible tendencies. Some, influenced by positivism, have emphasized the distinction between the historical world and what we say or write about it. Others, who adopt a "constructivist" viewpoint, have stressed the overlap between the historical process and narratives about that process. Most have treated the combination itself, the core of the ambiguity, as if it were a mere accident of vernacular parlance to be corrected by theory. What I hope to do is to show how much room there is to look at the production of history outside of the dichotomies that these positions suggest and reproduce.
zh: 词语不是概念，概念也不是词语：两者之间是历代累积的理论层。但理论建立在词语之上、用词语建成。因此，至少从古代起，“历史”一词日常用法中的歧义就引起许多思想家的注意，这并不奇怪。奇怪的是，历史理论处理这一基本歧义时的迟疑。的确，随着历史成为一种可辨识的职业，理论家们追随两种互不相容的倾向。一些人受实证主义影响，强调历史世界与我们关于它的言说或书写之间的区分。另一些人采取“建构主义”观点，强调历史过程与关于那个过程的叙述之间的重叠。大多数人把这种结合本身——歧义的核心——当作日常说法的偶然瑕疵，仿佛只须由理论来纠正。我希望做的，是展示在这些立场所暗示并再生产的二元对立之外，还有多大的空间来审视历史的生产。

en: One-sided Historicity
zh: 片面的历史性

en: Summaries of intellectual trends and subdisciplines always shortchange the various authors they somewhat compulsively regroup. I do not even attempt such a regrouping here. I hope that the following sketch is sufficient to show the limitations that I question.
zh: 对思潮与分支学科的概括，总是亏待了被它们近乎强制地归拢到一起的各位作者。我在这里甚至不尝试这种归拢。希望下面这幅速写足以展示我所质疑的那些局限。

en: Positivism has a bad name today, but at least some of that scorn is well deserved. As history solidified as a profession in the nineteenth century, scholars significantly influenced by positivist views tried to theorize the distinction between historical process and historical knowledge. Indeed, the professionalization of the discipline is partly premised on that distinction: the more distant the sociohistorical process is from its knowledge, the easier the claim to a "scientific" professionalism. Thus, historians and, more particularly, philosophers of history were proud to discover or reiterate instances where the distinction was supposedly indisputable because it was marked not only by semantic context, but by morphology or by the lexicon itself. zh: 实证主义今天名声不好，但至少其中一部分鄙夷是它应得的。随着历史在十九世纪固化为一门职业，深受实证主义观点影响的学者试图把历史过程与历史知识之间的区分理论化。的确，这门学科的职业化部分正是以那种区分为前提的：社会历史过程与对它的知识相距越远，宣称“科学的”职业性就越容易。于是，历史学家——尤其是历史哲学家——乐于发现或重申那些区分据说无可争辩的例证，因为标记这种区分的不仅是语义语境，还有形态或词汇本身。拉丁语中

en: The positivist position dominated Western scholarship enough to influence the vision of history among historians and philosophers who did not necessarily see themselves as positivists. Tenets of that vision still inform the public's sense of history in most of Europe and North America: the role of the historian is to reveal the past, to discover or, at least, approximate the truth. Within that viewpoint, power is unproblematic, irrelevant to the construction of the narrative as such. At best, history is a story about power, a story about those who won.
zh: 实证主义立场支配西方学术的程度，足以影响那些未必自认为实证主义者的历史学家和哲学家的历史观。这种历史观的信条，至今仍在塑造欧洲和北美大部分公众的历史感：历史学家的角色是揭示过去，是发现或至少逼近真相。在这种观点之内，权力不成问题，与叙述本身的建构无关。充其量，历史是一个关于权力的故事，一个关于赢家的故事。

en: The proposition that history is another form of fiction is almost as old as history itself, and the arguments used to defend it have varied greatly. As Tzvetan Todorov suggests, there is nothing new even in the claim that everything is an interpretation, except the euphoria that now surrounds the claim.

What I call the constructivist view of history is a particular version of these two propositions that has gained visibility in academe since the 1970s. It builds upon recent advances in critical theory, in the theory of the narrative and analytic philosophy. In its dominant version, it contends that the historical narrative bypasses the issue of truth by virtue of its form. Narratives are necessarily emplotted in a way that life is not. Thus they necessarily distort life whether or not the evidence upon which they are based could be proved correct. Within that viewpoint, history becomes one among many types of narratives with no particular distinction except for its pretense of truth.

Whereas the positivist view hides the tropes of power behind a naive epistemology, the constructivist one denies the autonomy of the sociohistorical process. Taken to its logical end point, constructivism views the historical narrative as one fiction among others.
zh: “历史是另一种虚构”这个命题几乎和历史本身一样古老，为它辩护的论据则变化多端。正如茨维坦·托多罗夫所指出的，就连“一切皆解释”这个说法也没什么新意，新的是如今围绕它的那种亢奋。
我所谓的历史建构主义观点，是这两个命题的一个特定版本，自1970年代以来在学界获得了能见度。它建立在批判理论、叙述理论和分析哲学晚近进展的基础上。在其主导版本中，它主张历史叙述凭借其形式绕开了真相问题。叙述必然被情节化，而生活不是。因此，无论叙述所依据的证据能否被证明为真，叙述都必然扭曲生活。在这种观点之内，历史成了众多叙述类型中的一种，唯一特殊之处在于它自称为真。
实证主义观点把权力的转义藏在一种天真的认识论背后，建构主义观点则否认社会历史过程的自主性。推到逻辑终点，建构主义把历史叙述看作众多虚构中的一种。

en: But what makes some narratives rather than others powerful enough to pass as accepted history if not historicity itself? If history is merely the story told by those who won, how did they win in the first place? And why don't all winners tell the same story?
zh: 可是，若不是历史性本身，又是什么使某些叙述而非另一些叙述强大到足以被当作公认的历史？如果历史不过是赢家讲的故事，他们当初是怎么赢的？为什么并非所有赢家都讲同一个故事？

en: Between Truth and Fiction
zh: 在真实与虚构之间

en: Each historical narrative renews a claim to truth.

If I write a story describing how U.S. troops entering a German prison at the end of World War II massacred five hundred Gypsies; if I claim this story is based on documents recently found in Soviet archives and corroborated by German sources, and if I fabricate such sources and publish my story as such, I have not written fiction, I have produced a fake. I have violated the rules that govern claims to historical truth.

That such rules are not the same in all times and all places has led many scholars to suggest that some societies (non-Western, of course) do not differentiate between fiction and history. That assertion reminds us of past debates among some Western observers about the languages of the peoples they colonized. Because these observers did not find grammar books or dictionaries among the so-called savages, because they could not understand or apply the grammatical rules that governed these languages, they promptly concluded that such rules did not exist.
zh: 每一部历史叙述都重申自己所述为真的主张。
如果我写一个故事，描述二战结束时进入一座德国监狱的美军如何屠杀了五百名吉普赛人；如果我声称这个故事依据的是新近在苏联档案中发现、并得到德国史料佐证的文件，而我伪造了这些史料并照此发表我的故事，那么我写的不是虚构，我制造的是赝品。我违反了主张历史真实所须遵守的规则。
这些规则并非在所有时代、所有地方都相同，这一点使许多学者提出：某些社会（当然是非西方社会）不区分虚构与历史。这种说法让我们想起过去一些西方观察者关于被殖民民族语言的争论。因为这些观察者在所谓野蛮人那里找不到语法书或词典，因为他们无法理解或运用支配这些语言的语法规则，他们就贸然断定这样的规则不存在。

en: As befits comparisons between the West and the many subaltern others it created for itself, the field was uneven from the start; the objects contrasted were eminently incomparable. The comparison unfairly juxtaposed a discourse about language and linguistic practice: the metalanguage of grammarians proved the existence of grammar in European languages; spontaneous speech proved its absence elsewhere. Some Europeans and their colonized students saw in this alleged absence of rules the infantile freedom that they came to associate with savagery, while others saw in it one more proof of the inferiority of non-whites. We now know that both sides were wrong; grammar functions in all languages. Could the same be said about history, or is history so infinitely malleable in some societies that it loses its differential claim to truth?
zh: 正如西方与它为自己制造的众多属下他者之间的比较所必然呈现的那样，这个场域从一开始就不平整；被对照的对象根本不可比。这种比较不公平地把关于语言的话语与语言实践并置：语法学家的元语言证明了欧洲语言中语法的存在；自发言语则证明了别处语法的缺席。一些欧洲人和他们被殖民的学生，从这种据说的规则缺席中看到了他们逐渐与野蛮联系起来的幼稚自由；另一些人则从中看到了非白人劣等性的又一证据。我们现在知道两边都错了；语法在所有语言中都起作用。历史是否也能这么说？还是说，历史在某些社会中可以无限揉捏，以至于失去了它不同于虚构的求真主张？

en: The classification of all non-Westerners as fundamentally non-historical is tied also to the assumption that history requires a linear and cumulative sense of time that allows the observer to isolate the past as a distinct entity. Yet Ibn Khaldhún fruitfully applied a cyclical view of time to the study of history. Further, the exclusive adherence to linear time by Western historians themselves, and the ensuing rejection of the people left "without history" both date from the nineteenth century.
Did the West have a history before 1800?
zh: 把所有非西方人归类为根本上非历史性的，还与一个假设绑在一起：历史需要一种线性、累积的时间感，使观察者能够把过去隔离为一个独立实体。然而伊本·赫勒敦曾富有成效地把循环时间观应用于历史研究。再者，西方历史学家自己对线性时间的独尊，以及随之而来的对被打发为“没有历史”的民族的拒斥，都始于十九世纪。
1800年以前，西方有历史吗？

en: The pernicious belief that epistemic validity matters only to Western-educated populations, either because others lack the proper sense of time or the proper sense of evidence, is belied by the use of
in a number of non-European languages.

An English approximation would be a rule forcing historians to distinguish grammatically between "I heard that it happened," "I saw it happen," or "I have obtained evidence that it happened" every time they use the verb "to happen." English, of course, has no such grammatical rule for assessing evidence. Does the fact that Tucuya has an elaborate system of evidentials predispose its Amazonian speakers to be better historians than most Englishmen?
zh: 有一种有害的信念：认识上的有效性只对受过西方教育的人群要紧，因为其他人要么缺乏恰当的时间感，要么缺乏恰当的证据感。许多非欧洲语言中传信语的使用驳斥了这种信念。
用英语近似地说，那就是一条规则，迫使历史学家每次使用动词“发生”时，都要在语法上区分“我听说它发生了”“我看见它发生”或“我获得了它发生的证据”。英语当然没有这样一条评估证据的语法规则。图库亚语拥有一套精细的传信语系统，这个事实是否就使其亚马逊使用者比大多数英国人更容易成为更好的历史学家？

en: Arjun Appadurai argues convincingly that rules about what he calls "the debatability of the past" operate in all societies.

Although these rules exhibit substantive variations in time and space, they all aim to guarantee a minimal credibility in history. Appadurai suggests a number of formal constraints that universally enforce that credibility and limit the character of historical debates: authority, continuity, depth, and interdependence. Nowhere is history infinitely susceptible to invention.
zh: 阿俊·阿帕杜莱令人信服地论证：关于他所谓“过去的可争辩性”的规则，在所有社会中都起作用。
尽管这些规则在时间和空间中表现出实质差异，它们都旨在保证历史中最低限度的可信性。阿帕杜莱提出了若干普遍强制这种可信性、并限定历史争论性质的形式约束：权威、连续性、深度与相互依存。没有任何地方的历史可以无限地被发明。

en: The need for a different kind of credibility sets the historical narrative apart from fiction. This need is both contingent and necessary. It is contingent inasmuch as some narratives go back and forth over the line between fiction and history, while others occupy an undefined position that seems to deny the very existence of a line. It is necessary inasmuch as, at some point, historically specific groups of humans must decide if a particular narrative belongs to history or to fiction. In other words, the epistemological break between history and fiction is always expressed concretely through the historically situated evaluation of specific narratives.
zh: 对另一种可信性的需要，使历史叙述区别于虚构。这种需要既是偶然的，又是必然的。说它偶然，是因为有些叙述在虚构与历史的界线上来回穿越，另一些则占据一个未定的位置，仿佛否认界线的存在。说它必然，是因为在某个时刻，处于具体历史中的人群必须判定某部叙述属于历史还是虚构。换言之，历史与虚构之间的认识论断裂，总是通过对具体叙述的历史处境化评价而具体地表达出来。

en: Is island cannibalism fact or fiction? Scholars have long tried to confirm or discredit some early Spanish colonizers' contention that Native Americans of the Antilles committed cannibalism.

Is the semantic association between Caribs, Cannibals, and Caliban based on more than European phantasms? Some scholars claim that the fantasy has reached such significance for the West that it matters little whether it is based on facts. Does this mean that the line between history and fiction is useless? As long as the conversation involves Europeans talking about dead Indians, the debate is merely academic.
zh: 岛屿食人是事实还是虚构？学者们长期试图证实或推翻早期西班牙殖民者的说法：安的列斯群岛的原住民实行食人。
加勒比人（Caribs）、食人者（Cannibals）与卡利班（Caliban）之间的语义关联，依据的难道不只是欧洲人的幻影？有些学者声称，这个幻想对西方已具有如此重大的意义，以至于它是否基于事实已无关紧要。这是否意味着历史与虚构之间的界线毫无用处？只要谈话还是欧洲人在谈论死去的印第安人，这场争论就只是学院式的。

en: Yet even dead Indians can return to haunt professional and amateur historians. The Inter-Tribal council of American Indians affirms that the remains of more than a thousand individuals, mostly Native American Catholics, are buried in grounds adjacent to the Alamo, in an old cemetery once linked to the Franciscan mission, but of which the most visible traces have disappeared. The council's efforts to have the sacredness of the grounds recognized by the state of Texas and the city of San Antonio have met only partial success. Still, they are impressive enough to threaten the control the organization that has custody of the Alamo, the Daughters of the Republic of Texas, holds over a historical site entrusted to them by the state since 1905.
zh: 然而，就连死去的印第安人也能回来纠缠职业与业余历史学家。美洲印第安人跨部落理事会确认：一千多人的遗骸——大多是原住民天主教徒——埋在阿拉莫旁边的一块地里，那是一座曾与方济各会传教站相连的老墓地，如今最显眼的痕迹已消失。理事会要求得克萨斯州和圣安东尼奥市承认这块地神圣性的努力只取得了部分成功。但这已足以威胁到阿拉莫保管组织——“得克萨斯共和国女儿会”——对一处自1905年起由州里委托其保管的历史遗址的控制权。

en: The debate over the grounds fits within a larger war that some observers have dubbed "the second battle of the Alamo." That larger controversy surrounds the 1836 siege of the compound by Santa Anna's forces. Is that battle a moment of glory during which freedom-loving Anglos, outnumbered but undaunted, spontaneously chose to fight until death rather than surrender to a corrupt Mexican dictator? Or is it a brutal example of U.S. expansionism, the story of a few white predators taking over what was sacred territory and half-willingly providing, with their death, the alibi for a well-planned annexation? So phrased the debate evokes issues that have divided a few historians and inhabitants of Texas over the last twenty years. But with San Antonio's population now composed of 56 percent nominal Hispanics, many of whom also acknowledge some Native American ancestry, "the second battle of the Alamo" has literally reached the streets. Demonstrations, parades, editorials, and demands for various municipal or court orders—including one blocking the streets now leading to the Alamo—punctuate the debate between increasingly angry parties.
zh: 围绕这块地的争论，属于一场被一些观察者称为“阿拉莫第二战役”的更大战争。那场更大的争议围绕1836年圣安纳军队对这座院落的围攻。那场战斗是一个荣耀时刻——热爱自由的盎格鲁白人寡不敌众却毫不畏惧，自发选择战斗至死，而不向一个腐败的墨西哥独裁者投降？还是美国扩张主义的一个残暴例证——几个白人掠夺者夺取了神圣的领土，并半自愿地用自己的死，为一场蓄谋已久的吞并提供借口？这样表述的争论，唤起了过去二十年间分裂一些历史学家和得克萨斯居民的那些问题。但随着圣安东尼奥人口中如今56%是名义上的西班牙裔，其中许多人还承认有原住民血统，“阿拉莫第二战役”已字面意义上地打到了街头。示威、游行、社论，以及要求各种市政令或法院令的呼声——包括一道封锁如今通往阿拉莫街道的命令——此起彼伏，穿插在日益愤怒的各方之间的争论中。

en: In the heated context of this debate, advocates on both sides are questioning factual statements, the accuracy of which mattered to few half a century ago. "Facts," both trivial or prominent in relative isolation, are questioned or heralded by each camp.
zh: 在这场争论的白热化语境中，双方的辩护者都在质疑一些事实陈述，而半个世纪前几乎没人在乎这些陈述是否准确。这些“事实”相对孤立地看有的微不足道，有的突出醒目，各阵营对它们或质疑，或大加宣扬。

en: Historians had long questioned the veracity of some of the events in Alamo narratives, most notably the story of the line on the ground. According to that story, when it became clear that the choice for the 189 Alamo occupants was between escape and certain death at the Mexicans' hands, commandant William Barret Travis drew a line on the ground. He then asked all those willing to fight to the death to cross it. Supposedly, everyone crossed—except of course the man who conveniently escaped to tell the story. Texas historians, and especially Texas-based authors of textbooks and popular history, long concurred that this particular narrative was only "a good story," and that "it doesn't really matter whether it is true or not."

Such remarks were made before the current constructivist wave by people who otherwise believed that facts are facts and nothing but facts. But in a context where the courage of the men who stayed at the Alamo is openly questioned, the line on the ground is suddenly among the many "facts" now submitted to a test of credibility.
zh: 历史学家早就质疑过阿拉莫叙述中某些事件的真实性，最著名的是地上划线的故事。按那个故事的说法，当189名阿拉莫占据者面临的抉择清楚地摆在逃跑与必死于墨西哥人之手之间时，指挥官威廉·巴雷特·特拉维斯在地上划了一条线，然后请所有愿意战斗至死的人跨过它。据说所有人都跨了过去——当然，除了那个恰好逃出去讲故事的人。得克萨斯历史学家，尤其是得克萨斯本地的教科书与通俗历史作者，长期一致认为这个特定叙述只是“一个好故事”，“它是真是假其实无所谓”。
说这话的人处于当前建构主义浪潮之前，他们本来相信事实就是事实，仅仅是事实。但在一个留守阿拉莫者的勇气受到公开质疑的语境里，地上那条线突然成了如今被提交可信性检验的众多“事实”之一。

en: The list is endless.

Where exactly was the cemetery, and are the remains still there? Are tourist visits to the Alamo violating the religious rights of the dead and should the state of Texas intervene? Did the state itself ever pay the Roman Catholic Church the agreed-upon price for the chapel of the Alamo and, if not, are not the custodians usurpers of a historical landmark? Did James Bowie, one of the white American leaders, bury a stolen treasure in the site? If so, is that the real reason why the occupants chose to fight or, conversely, did Bowie try to negotiate in order to save both his life and the treasure? In short, how much was greed, rather than patriotism, central to the Alamo battle? Did the besieged mistakenly believe that reinforcement was on its way and, if so, how much can we believe in their courage? Did Davy Crockett die during the battle or after the battle? Did he try to surrender? Did he really wear a coonskin cap?
zh: 清单无穷无尽。

墓地究竟在哪里，遗骸还在不在那里？游客参观阿拉莫是否侵犯了死者的宗教权利，得克萨斯州该不该干预？州里究竟有没有向罗马天主教会支付阿拉莫小教堂的约定价款，如果没有，保管者难道不是一处历史地标的僭夺者？白人美国领袖之一詹姆斯·鲍伊有没有在现场埋过一批偷来的财宝？如果有，那是不是占据者选择战斗的真正原因；或者反过来说，鲍伊是否曾试图谈判，以保住自己的性命和财宝？总之，在阿拉莫战斗中，贪婪而非爱国，在多大程度上是核心？被围者是否误以为援军正在路上，如果是，他们的勇气还能让我们相信多少？戴维·克罗克特死于战斗之中还是战斗之后？他有没有试图投降？他是不是真戴过一顶浣熊皮帽？

en: That last question may sound the most trivial of a rather bizarre list; but it appears less trifling and not at all bizarre when we note that the Alamo shrine is Texas's main tourist attraction, drawing some three million visitors a year. Now that local voices have become loud enough to question the innocence of a little

wearing a Davy cap, mom and dad may think twice about buying one, and the custodians of history shiver, afraid that the past is catching up too fast with the present. In the context of that controversy, it suddenly matters how real Davy was.
zh: 最后一个问题在这份相当古怪的清单里也许听起来最琐碎；但当我们注意到阿拉莫圣地是得克萨斯的头号旅游吸引物、每年吸引约三百万游客时，它就不那么琐碎、也一点也不古怪了。既然本地的声音已响亮到足以质疑一个戴戴维帽的小“外国佬”（gringo）是否无辜，爸爸妈妈买帽子前可能就要三思，而历史的保管者们则不寒而栗，生怕过去追赶现在的速度太快。在那场争议的语境中，戴维有多真实，突然变得要紧起来。

en: The lesson of the debate is clear. At some stage, for reasons that are themselves historical, most often spurred by controversy, collectivities experience the need to impose a test of credibility on certain events and narratives because it matters
whether these events are true or false, whether these stories are fact or fiction.
zh: 这场争论的教训是清楚的。在某个阶段，出于本身即历史性的原因——最常由争议激发——群体会感到需要对某些事件和叙述施加可信性检验，因为这些事件是真是假、这些故事是事实还是虚构，对
要紧。

en: That it matters to them does not necessarily mean that it matters to us. But how far can we carry our isolationism? Does it really not matter whether or not the dominant narrative of the Jewish Holocaust is true or false? Does it really not make a difference whether or not the leaders of Nazi Germany actually planned and supervised the death of six million Jews?
zh: 对他们要紧，未必意味着对我们也要紧。但我们的孤立主义能走多远？关于犹太人大屠杀的主导叙述是真是假，难道真的无所谓？纳粹德国的领导人是否确实策划并监督了对六百万犹太人的屠杀，难道真的没有分别？

en: The associates of the Institute for Historical Review maintain that the Holocaust narrative matters, but they also maintain that it is false. They generally agree that Jews were victimized during World War II, and some even accept that the Holocaust was a tragedy. However, most profess to set the record straight on three main issues: the reported number of six million Jews killed by the Nazis; the systematic Nazi plan for the extermination of Jews; the existence of "gas chambers" for mass murders.

Revisionists claim there is no irrefutable evidence to back any of these central "facts" of the dominant Holocaust narrative which serves only to perpetuate various state policies in the United States, Europe, and Israel.
zh: “历史评论研究所”（Institute for Historical Review）的同人们坚持大屠杀叙述事关紧要，但也坚持它是假的。他们大体同意犹太人在二战中受到迫害，有些人甚至承认大屠杀是一场悲剧。然而，大多数人声称要在三个主要问题上澄清记录：据称被纳粹杀害的六百万犹太人这个数字；纳粹系统性灭绝犹太人的计划；是否存在用于大规模屠杀的“毒气室”。
修正主义者声称，没有任何不可辩驳的证据支持主导大屠杀叙述的这些核心“事实”，而那套叙述只不过是在延续美国、欧洲和以色列的各种国家政策。

en: Revisionist theses on the Holocaust have been refuted by a number of authors. Historian Pierre Vidal-Naquet, whose own mother died at Auschwitz, has used his repeated rebuttals of revisionist theses to raise powerful questions on the relation between scholarship and political responsibility. Jean-Pierre Pressac, himself a former revisionist, documents better than any other historian the German death machinery. Deborah Lipstadt's most recent book on the subject examines the political motivations of the revisionists in order to launch an ideological critique of revisionism. To that latter kind of critique, the revisionists reply that they are historians: why should their motives matter if they follow "the customary methods of historical criticism"? We can't dismiss heliocentric theory just because Copernicus apparently hated the Catholic Church.
zh: 关于大屠杀的修正主义论点已被许多作者驳倒。历史学家皮埃尔·维达尔-纳凯的母亲本人死于奥斯维辛，他利用自己一次次对修正主义论点的反驳，提出了关于学术与政治责任之关系的有力问题。让-皮埃尔·普雷萨克本人曾是修正主义者，他对德国死亡机器的文献记录比任何其他历史学家都更翔实。黛博拉·利普斯塔特关于这一主题的最新著作考察修正主义者的政治动机，以便发起对修正主义的意识形态批判。对后一种批判，修正主义者回答说他们是历史学家：如果他们遵循“史料批判的通行方法”，他们的动机为什么要紧？我们不能仅仅因为哥白尼显然讨厌天主教会，就否定日心说。
body.review: 本段原印作 Jean-Pierre Pressac，本章注13所引《奥斯维辛的焚尸炉》署名 Jean-Claude Pressac，均按各自原文保留。

en: The revisionists' claimed adherence to empiricist procedures provides a perfect case to test the limits of historical constructionism.

The immediate political and moral stakes of Holocaust narratives for a number of constituencies worldwide, and the competing strength and loudness of these constituencies in the United States and in Europe leave the constructivists both politically and theoretically naked. For the only logical constructivist position on the Holocaust debate is to deny that there is matter to debate. Constructivists must claim that it does not really matter whether or not there were gas chambers, whether the death toll was one or six million, or whether the genocide was planned. And indeed, constructivist Hayden White came dangerously close to suggesting that the main relevance of the dominant Holocaust narrative is that it serves to legitimate the policies of the state of Israel.
White later qualified his extreme constructivist stance and now espouses a much more modest relativism.
zh: 修正主义者自称遵循经验主义程序，这为检验历史建构论的限度提供了一个绝佳案例。

大屠杀叙述对世界各地许多群体具有直接的政治与道德利害，而这些群体在美国和欧洲相互竞争的力量与声量，使建构主义者在政治上和理论上都被剥得精光。因为建构主义者在大屠杀争论上唯一合乎逻辑的立场，就是否认存在可争之事。建构主义者必须声称：有没有毒气室、死亡人数是一百万还是六百万、种族灭绝是否经过策划，都真的无所谓。而事实上，建构主义者海登·怀特就曾危险地接近于暗示：主导大屠杀叙述的主要意义，在于它为以色列国的政策提供正当性。
怀特后来给自己原本极端的建构主义立场加了限定，如今持一种温和得多的相对主义。

en: But how much can we reduce what happened to what is said to have happened? If six million do not really matter, would two million be enough, or would some of us settle for three hundred thousand? If meaning is totally severed from a referent "out there," if there is no cognitive purpose, nothing to be proved or disproved, what then is the point of the story? White's answer is clear: to establish moral authority. But why bother with the Holocaust or plantation slavery, Pol Pot, or the French Revolution, when we already have Little Red Riding Hood?
zh: 但是，我们能在多大程度上把“发生了什么”化约为“据说发生了什么”？如果六百万真的无所谓，两百万够不够？或者我们中有些人会不会满足于三十万？如果意义与“外部那里”的指涉物完全切断，如果没有认识目的，没有什么要证实或证伪，那么故事的意义何在？怀特的回答很明确：确立道德权威。可是，既然我们已经有了小红帽，何必还要费心于大屠杀、种植园奴隶制、波尔布特或法国大革命？

en: Constructivism's dilemma is that

children: while it can point to hundreds of stories that illustrate its general claim that narratives are produced, it cannot give a full account of the production of any single narrative.

en: For either we would all share the same stories of legitimation, or the reasons why a specific story matters to a specific population are themselves historical. To state that a particular narrative legitimates particular policies is to refer implicitly to a "true" account of these policies through time, an account which itself can take the form of another narrative. But to admit the possibility of this second narrative is, in turn, to admit that the historical process has some autonomy vis-à-vis the narrative. It is to admit that as ambiguous and contingent as it is, the boundary between what happened and that which is said to have happened is necessary.
zh: 建构主义的两难在于：

children: 尽管它能指出成百上千个故事来例证其“叙述是被生产的”这一一般主张，它却无法完整说明任何单一叙述的生产。

zh: 因为要么我们全都共享同样的合法化故事，要么某个特定故事对特定人群之所以要紧的原因本身就是历史性的。断言某部叙述为某些政策赋予正当性，就是隐含地指涉一份关于这些政策随时间演变的“真实”记录，而这份记录本身又可以采取另一部叙述的形式。但承认这第二部叙述的可能性，反过来就是承认历史过程相对叙述具有某种自主性。这就是承认：“发生了什么”与“据说发生了什么”之间的边界尽管歧义而偶然，却是必然的。

en: It is not that some societies distinguish between fiction and history and others do not. Rather, the difference is in the range of narratives that specific collectivities must put to their own tests of historical credibility because of the stakes involved in these narratives.
zh: 问题不在于有些社会区分虚构与历史、另一些不区分。差别在于：由于叙述中涉及的利害，特定群体必须把哪些范围的叙述提交给自己的历史可信性检验。

en: Single-site Historicity
zh: 单一场所的历史性

en: We would be wrong to think that such stakes proceed naturally from the importance of the original event. The widespread notion of history as reminiscence of important past experiences is misleading. The model itself is well known: history is to a collectivity as remembrance is to an individual, the more or less conscious retrieval of past experiences stored in memory. Its numerous variations aside, we can call it, for short, the storage model of memory-history.
zh: 如果以为这些利害自然地来自原初事件的重要性，那就错了。把历史视为对重要过去经验的回忆，这种流行观念是误导性的。这个模型本身众所周知：历史之于群体，犹如记忆之于个人，是对存储在记忆中的过去经验或多或少有意识的提取。撇开它的众多变体不论，我们可以简称为记忆-历史的存储模型。

en: The first problem with the storage model is its age, the antiquated science upon which it rests. The model assumes a view of knowledge as recollection, which goes back to Plato, a view now disputed by philosophers and cognitive scientists. Further, the vision of individual memory on which it draws has been strongly questioned by researchers of various stripes since at least the end of the nineteenth century. Within that vision, memories are discrete representations stored in a cabinet, the contents of which are generally accurate and accessible at will. Recent research has questioned all these assumptions. Remembering is not always a process of summoning representations of what happened. Tying a shoe involves memory, but few of us engage in an explicit recall of images every time we routinely tie our shoes. Whether or not the distinction between implicit and explicit memory involves different memory systems, the fact that such systems are inextricably linked in practice may be one more reason why explicit memories change. At any rate, there is evidence that the contents of our cabinet are neither fixed nor accessible at will.
zh: 存储模型的第一个问题是它的年代，是它所依赖的过时科学。这个模型预设了一种把知识视为回忆的观点，可上溯到柏拉图，而如今哲学家和认知科学家已在质疑这种观点。再者，它所借重的个体记忆图景，至少从十九世纪末以来就受到各路研究者的强烈质疑。在那种图景中，记忆是储存在柜子里的离散表征，柜中之物大体准确，可随意取用。晚近研究质疑了所有这些预设。记忆并不总是一个召唤“发生了什么”之表征的过程。系鞋带涉及记忆，但我们没几个人每次例行系鞋带时都明确回忆图像。无论内隐记忆与外显记忆的区分是否涉及不同的记忆系统，这些系统在实践中不可分割地纠缠在一起这一事实，也许正是外显记忆会变化的又一个原因。无论如何，有证据表明，我们柜子里的内容既不固定，也不能随意取用。

en: Further, were such contents complete, they would not form a history. Consider a monologue describing in sequence all of an individual's recollections. It would sound as a meaningless cacophony even to the narrator. Further, it is at least possible that events otherwise significant to the life trajectory were not known to the individual at the time of occurrence and cannot be told as remembered experiences. The individual can only remember the revelation, not the event itself. I may remember that I went to Japan without remembering what it felt like to be in Japan. I may remember being told that my parents took me to Japan when I was six months old. But then, is it only the revelation that belongs to my life history? Can we confidently exclude from one's history all events not experienced or not yet revealed, including, for instance, an adoption at the time of birth? An adoption might provide a crucial perspective on episodes that actually occurred before its revelation. The revelation itself may affect the narrator's future memory of events that happened
zh: 再者，即使这些内容完整无缺，它们也构不成一部历史。设想一段独白，依次描述一个人的全部回忆。即使对叙述者本人，它听起来也会像一堆无意义的杂音。再者，至少有可能：某些对人生轨迹本来重要的事件，当事人在事件发生时并不知情，因而无法作为被记忆的经验来讲述。当事人只能记得那个揭示，而不是事件本身。我可能记得我去过日本，却不记得身在日本是什么感受。我可能记得别人告诉我，我六个月大时父母带我去过日本。可是，难道只有那个揭示属于我的生命史？我们能否有把握地把一切未曾经历或尚未揭示的事件——比如出生时的一次收养——都排除在一个人的历史之外？一次收养可能为揭示之前实际发生的种种片段提供一个关键视角。揭示本身可能影响叙述者日后对发生在“之前”的事件的记忆。

en: If memories as individual history are constructed, even in this minimal sense, how can the past they retrieve be fixed? The storage model has no answer to that problem. Both its popular and scholarly versions assume the independent existence of a fixed past and posit memory as the retrieval of that content. But the past does not exist independently from the present. Indeed, the past is only past because there is a present, just as I can point to something
only because I am
But nothing is inherently over there or here. In that sense, the past has no content. The past—or, more accurately, pastness—is a position. Thus, in no way can we identify the past

Leaving aside for now the fact that my knowledge that I once went to Japan, however derived, may not be of the same nature as remembering what it was like to be in Japan, the model assumes that both kinds of information exist
prior to my retrieval. But how do I retrieve them as past without prior knowledge or memory of what constitutes pastness?
zh: 如果作为个人历史的记忆是被建构的——哪怕只是在这种最低限度的意义上——它们所提取的过去又怎么会是固定的？存储模型对这个问题没有答案。它的通俗版和学术版都预设一个固定过去的独立存在，并把记忆设定为对那个内容的提取。但过去并不独立于现在而存在。的确，过去之所以是过去，只因为有一个现在，正如我只能因为我在“这里”才能指着“那里”的某物。但没有什么东西天生就在那里或这里。在这个意义上，过去没有内容。过去——或者更准确地说，过去性——是一个位置。因此，我们绝不可能把过去“作为过去”来识别。暂且不论这一点：我知道我曾去过日本，无论这知识从何而来，可能与记得身在日本是什么感受性质不同；模型预设这两类信息在我提取之前就“作为过去”存在。可是，如果没有关于什么构成过去性的先行知识或记忆，我如何把它们作为过去提取出来？

en: The problems of determining what belongs to the past multiply tenfold when that past is said to be collective. Indeed, when the memory-history equation is transferred to a collectivity, methodological individualism adds its weight to the inherent difficulties of the storage model. We may want to assume for purposes of description that the life history of an individual starts with birth. But when does the life of a collectivity start? At what point do we set the beginning of the past to be retrieved? How do we decide—and how does the collectivity decide—which events to include and which to exclude? The storage model assumes not only the past to be remembered but the collective subject that does the remembering. The problem with this dual assumption is that the constructed past itself is constitutive of the collectivity.
zh: 当那个过去被说成是集体过去时，判定什么属于过去的问题就增加了十倍。的确，当记忆-历史等式被移用到群体上时，方法论个人主义又给存储模型的固有困难加了码。为了描述方便，我们不妨假设个人的生命史始于出生。但群体的生命何时开始？我们把待提取过去的起点定在哪里？我们如何决定——群体又如何决定——哪些事件纳入、哪些排除？存储模型不仅预设了待记忆的过去，还预设了执行记忆的集体主体。这个双重预设的问题在于：被建构的过去本身正是群体的构成要素。

en: Do Europeans and white Americans remember discovering the New World? Neither Europe as we now know it, nor whiteness as we now experience it, existed as such in 1492. Both are constitutive of this retrospective entity we now call the West, without which the "discovery" is unthinkable in its present form. Can the citizens of Quebec, whose license plates proudly state "I remember," actually retrieve memories of the French colonial state? Can Macedonians, whoever they may be, recall the early conflicts and promises of panhellenism? Can anybody anywhere actually remember the first mass conversions of Serbians to Christianity? In these cases, as in many others, the collective subjects who supposedly remember did not exist as such at the time of the events they claim to remember. Rather, their constitution as subjects goes hand in hand with the continuous creation of the past. As such, they do not succeed such a past: they are its contemporaries.
zh: 欧洲人和美国白人记得自己发现新大陆吗？1492年，我们今天所知的欧洲和我们今天所体验的白人性，都不以这样的形态存在。两者都是我们今天称为西方这个回溯性实体的构成要素，没有它，“发现”以其现有形式是不可构想的。车牌上自豪地写着“我记着”的魁北克公民，真能提取关于法兰西殖民国家的记忆吗？马其顿人——无论他们是谁——能回想起泛希腊主义早期的冲突与承诺吗？任何地方的任何人，真能记得塞尔维亚人最初大规模皈依基督教吗？在这些例子和许多其他例子中，据说是记忆主体的集体主体，在他们声称记忆的事件发生时并不以这样的形态存在。毋宁说，他们作为主体的构成，与过去的持续创造携手并进。因此，他们不是那个过去的继承者：他们是它的同代人。

en: Even when the historical continuities are unquestionable, in no way can we assume a simple correlation between the magnitude of events as they happened and their relevance for the generations that inherit them through history. The comparative study of slavery in the Americas provides an engaging example that what we often call the "legacy of the past" may not be anything bequeathed by the past itself.
zh: 即使历史连续性无可置疑，我们也绝不能假设：事件发生时的规模，和后世通过历史继承这些事件时所感受到的切身意义，两者之间存在简单的对应关系。美洲奴隶制的比较研究提供了一个引人入胜的例证：我们常说的“过去的遗产”，可能根本不是过去本身遗赠的东西。

en: At first glance, it would seem obvious that the historical relevance of slavery in the United States proceeds from the horrors of the past. That past is constantly evoked as the starting point of an ongoing traumatism and as a necessary explanation to current inequalities suffered by blacks. I would be the last to deny that plantation slavery was a traumatic experience that left strong scars throughout the Americas. But the experience of African-Americans outside of the United States challenges the direct correlation between past traumas and historical relevance.
zh: 乍看之下，美国奴隶制的历史相关性来自过去的恐怖，这似乎显而易见。那个过去不断被唤起，作为持续创伤的起点，作为黑人当下所受不平等的必要解释。我绝不会否认种植园奴隶制是一段创伤经验，在整个美洲留下深深的伤疤。但美国以外的美洲非洲裔群体的经历，挑战了过去创伤与历史相关性之间的直接关联。

en: In the context of the hemisphere, the United States imported a relatively small number of enslaved Africans both before and after its independence. During four centuries, the slave trade delivered at least ten million slaves to the New World. Enslaved Africans worked and died in the Caribbean a century before the settlement of Jamestown, Virginia. Brazil, the territory where slavery lasted longest, received the lion's share of the African slaves, nearly four million. The Caribbean region as a whole imported even more slaves than Brazil, spread among the colonies of various European powers. Still, imports were high among individual Caribbean territories, especially the sugar islands. Thus the French Caribbean island of Martinique, a tiny territory less than one-fourth the size of Long Island, imported more slaves than all the U.S. states combined.

To be sure, by the early nineteenth century, the United States had more Creole slaves than any other American country, but this number was due to natural increase. Still, both in terms of its duration and in terms of the number of individuals involved, in no way can we say that the magnitude of U.S. slavery outdid that of Brazil or the Caribbean.
zh: 放在整个半球的语境中，美国在独立前后输入的非洲奴隶都相对较少。四个世纪里，奴隶贸易向新世界输送了至少一千万奴隶。早在弗吉尼亚詹姆斯敦定居点建立前一个世纪，被奴役的非洲人就在加勒比劳作和死去。巴西是奴隶制延续最久的领土，得到了非洲奴隶的最大份额，将近四百万。加勒比地区整体输入的奴隶比巴西还多，分散在各欧洲列强的殖民地中。而且，单个加勒比领土的输入量也很高，尤其是那些糖岛。于是，法属加勒比岛屿马提尼克——一块不到长岛四分之一大的小领土——输入的奴隶比美国所有州加起来还多。
诚然，到十九世纪初，美国的克里奥尔（本地出生）奴隶比任何其他美洲国家都多，但这个数字来自自然增长。尽管如此，无论就持续时间还是就涉及的人数而言，我们都绝不能说美国奴隶制的规模超过了巴西或加勒比。

en: Second, slavery was at least as significant to the daily life of Brazilian and Caribbean societies as to U.S. society as a whole. The British and French sugar islands in particular, from seventeenth-century Barbados and Jamaica to eighteenth-century Saint-Domingue and Martinique, were not simply societies that had slaves: they were

Slavery defined their economic, social, and cultural organization: it was their raison d'être. The people who lived there, free or not, lived there because there were slaves. The northern equivalent would be for the whole continental United States to look like the state of Alabama at the peak of its cotton career.
zh: 第二，奴隶制对巴西和加勒比社会日常生活的意义，至少不亚于它对美国社会整体的意义。尤其是英法两国的糖岛，从十七世纪的巴巴多斯和牙买加，到十八世纪的圣多明各和马提尼克，不只是拥有奴隶的社会：它们是“奴隶社会”。奴隶制规定了它们的经济、社会和文化组织：它是它们的存在理由（raison d'être）。住在那里的人，无论自由与否，都是因为那里有奴隶才住在那里。北方的对应情形，就相当于整个美国大陆都像棉花事业巅峰期的阿拉巴马州。

en: Third, we need not assume that human suffering can be measured to affirm that the slaves' material conditions were no better outside the United States than within its borders. Allegations of paternalism notwithstanding, we know that U.S. masters were no more humane than their Brazilian or Caribbean counterparts. But we know also that the human toll of slavery, both physical and cultural, was intimately tied to the exigencies of production, notably the work regimen. Working conditions generally imposed lower life expectancy, higher death rates, and much lower birth rates among Caribbean and Brazilian slaves than among their U.S. counterparts.
From that viewpoint, sugarcane was the slaves' most sadistic tormentor.
zh: 第三，我们无需假设人类苦难可以计量，也能断言：美国境外的奴隶物质条件并不比境内更好。尽管有家长制的美化说法，我们知道美国奴隶主并不比巴西或加勒比的同行更人道。但我们也知道，奴隶制的人力代价——无论是身体上还是文化上——与生产的苛求、尤其是劳动规程紧密相连。劳动条件通常使加勒比和巴西奴隶的预期寿命更低、死亡率更高、出生率远低于美国奴隶。
从这个角度看，甘蔗是奴隶最施虐成性的折磨者。

en: In short, there is a mass of evidence big enough to uphold a modest empirical claim: The impact of slavery as what actually happened cannot in any way be said to have been stronger in the United States than in Brazil and the Caribbean. But then, why is both the symbolic relevance of slavery as trauma and the analytical relevance of slavery as sociohistorical explanation so much more prevalent today in the United States than in Brazil or the Caribbean?
zh: 总之，有大量证据足以支持一个温和的经验主张：作为实际发生之事的奴隶制，其冲击绝不能说在美国比在巴西和加勒比更强。可是，为什么奴隶制作为创伤在象征上所占的地位，以及它在解释社会历史时的分析价值，今天都在美国比在巴西或加勒比更受重视？

en: Part of the answer may be the way U.S. slavery ended: a Civil War for which more whites seem to blame the slaves than Abraham Lincoln—whose own motives in the enterprise remain otherwise contested. Part of the answer may be the fate of the slaves' descendants, but that itself is not an issue of "the past." The perpetuation of U.S. racism is less a legacy of slavery than a modern phenomenon renewed by generations of white immigrants whose own ancestors were likely engaged in forced labor, at one time or another, in the hinterlands of Europe.
zh: 部分答案也许在于美国奴隶制的结束方式：一场内战，而更多白人似乎把这场战争归咎于奴隶，而不是亚伯拉罕·林肯——林肯本人在这件事上的动机另外仍有争议。部分答案也许在于奴隶后裔的命运，但那本身不是“过去”的问题。美国种族主义的延续，与其说是奴隶制的遗产，不如说是一种现代现象，被一代代白人移民不断更新，而这些移民自己的祖先很可能曾在欧洲腹地某个时期遭受过强制劳役。

en: Indeed, not all blacks who witnessed slavery believed that it was a legacy of which they and their children would forever carry the burden.

Half a century after Emancipation, slavery was not a major theme among white historians either, albeit for different reasons. U.S. historiography, for reasons perhaps not too different from its Brazilian counterpart, produced its own silences on African-American slavery. Earlier in this century, there were blacks and whites in North America who argued over both the symbolic and analytical relevance of slavery for the present they were living.
Such debates suggest that historical relevance does not proceed directly from the original impact of an event, or its mode of inscription, or even the continuity of that inscription.
zh: 的确，并非所有目睹过奴隶制的黑人都相信，那是一份他们和子孙要永远背负的遗产。
解放半个世纪后，奴隶制在白人历史学家那里也不是主要题目，尽管原因不同。美国史学——原因也许与其巴西同行相差无几——在美国非洲裔遭受奴役的问题上制造了自己的沉默。本世纪早些时候，北美曾有黑人和白人争论奴隶制对他们所生活的当下在象征和分析上的意义。
这类争论表明：历史相关性并不直接来自事件的原始冲击，或它的铭刻方式，甚至也不来自那种铭刻的连续性。

en: Debates about the Alamo, the Holocaust, or the significance of U.S. slavery involve not only professional historians but ethnic and religious leaders, political appointees, journalists, and various associations within civil society as well as independent citizens, not all of whom are activists. This variety of narrators is one of many indications that theories of history have a rather limited view of the field of historical production. They grossly underestimate the size, the relevance, and the complexity of the overlapping sites where history is produced, notably outside of academia.
zh: 关于阿拉莫、大屠杀或美国奴隶制意义的争论，参与者不仅有职业历史学家，还有族群与宗教领袖、政治任命官员、记者、公民社会中的各种社团，以及独立公民——他们并不都是活动家。叙述者的这种多样性，是众多迹象之一，表明历史理论对历史生产场域的看法相当狭隘。它们严重低估了历史得以生产的那些交叠场所的规模、相关性和复杂性，尤其是学院之外的场所。

en: The strength of the historical guild varies from one society to the next. Even in highly complex societies where the weight of the guild is significant, never does the historians' production constitute a closed corpus. Rather, that production interacts not only with the work of other academics, but importantly also with the history produced outside of the universities. Thus, the thematic awareness of history is not activated only by recognized academics. We are all amateur historians with various degrees of awareness about our production. We also learn history from similar amateurs. Universities and university presses are not the only loci of production of the historical narrative. Books sell even better than coonskin caps at the Alamo gift shop, to which half a dozen titles by amateur historians bring more than $400,000 a year. As Marc Ferro argues, history has many hearths and academics are not the sole history teachers in the land.
zh: 历史行会的力量因社会而异。即使在行会分量很重的高度复杂社会里，历史学家的产品也从不构成一个封闭的总体。毋宁说，那种产品不仅与其他学者的工作互动，更重要的是也与大学之外生产的历史互动。因此，对历史的主题意识并非只由公认的学者激活。我们都是业余历史学家，对自己产品的自觉程度各不相同。我们也从类似的业余者那里学习历史。大学和大学出版社不是历史叙述的唯一生产场所。在阿拉莫礼品店，书卖得比浣熊皮帽还好，业余历史学家写的约六种书每年带来四十多万美元。正如马克·费罗所论，历史有许多炉灶，学者不是这片土地上唯一的历史教师。

en: Most Europeans and North Americans learn their first history lessons through media that have not been subjected to the standards set by peer reviews, university presses, or doctoral committees. Long before average citizens read the historians who set the standards of the day for colleagues and students, they access history through celebrations, site and museum visits, movies, national holidays, and primary school books. To be sure, the views they learn there are, in turn, sustained, modified, or challenged by scholars involved in primary research. As history continues to solidify professionally, as historians become increasingly quick at modifying their targets and refining their tools for investigation, the impact of academic history increases, even if indirectly.
zh: 大多数欧洲人和北美人的第一堂历史课，来自未经同行评审、大学出版社或博士委员会标准检验的媒介。普通公民早在读到那些为同行和学生设定当日标准的历史学家之前，就通过庆典、遗址与博物馆参观、电影、国庆假日和小学课本接触历史了。诚然，他们在那里学到的观点，反过来又会被从事一手研究的学者支持、修改或挑战。随着历史继续在职业上固化，随着历史学家越来越快地调整目标、打磨研究工具，学院史学的影响在增加，哪怕是间接的。

en: But let us not forget how fragile, how limited, and how recent that apparent hegemony may be. Let us not forget that, quite recently, in many parts of the United States national and world history prolonged a providential narrative with strong religious undertones. The history of the world then started with Creation, for which the date was supposedly well known, and continued with Manifest Destiny, as befits a country privileged by Divine Providence. American social science has yet to discard the belief in U.S. exceptionalism that permeated its birth and its evolution.
Likewise, academic professionalism has not yet silenced creationist history, which is still alive in enclaves within the school system.
zh: 但别忘了，那种表面霸权可能多么脆弱、多么有限、多么晚近。别忘了，就在不久之前，美国许多地方的国史和世界史还在延续一种带有浓厚宗教底色的天意叙述。那时世界史始于创世——日期据说是确知的——接着是天定命运，恰如一个蒙神意眷顾的国家之所宜。美国社会科学尚未丢弃渗透其诞生与演进的美国例外论信念。
同样，学院职业主义也尚未让神创论历史沉默，它仍在学校系统的一些飞地里活着。

en: That school system may not have the last word on any issue, but its limited efficiency cuts both ways. From the mid 1950s to the late 1960s, Americans learned more about the history of colonial America and the American West from movies and television than from scholarly books. Remember the Alamo? That was a history lesson delivered by John Wayne on the screen. Davy Crockett was a television character who became a significant historical figure rather than the obverse.

Before and after Hollywood's long commitment to the history of cowboys and pioneers, comic books rather than textbooks, country songs rather than chronological tables filled the gaps left by the westerns. Then as now, American children and quite a few young males elsewhere learned to thematize parts of that history by playing cowboys and Indians.
zh: 学校系统在任何问题上也许都没有最终发言权，但它有限的效力是双向的。从1950年代中期到1960年代末，美国人从电影和电视里学到的殖民时期美洲史和美国西部史，比从学术著作里学到的更多。“铭记阿拉莫”？那是约翰·韦恩在银幕上讲授的一堂历史课。戴维·克罗克特是一个电视角色变成了重要历史人物，而不是反过来。
在好莱坞长期致力于牛仔与拓荒者历史之前和之后，填补西部片留下空白的，是漫画书而不是教科书，是乡村歌曲而不是年表。那时和现在一样，美国儿童和其他地方不少年轻男性，通过玩“牛仔与印第安人”游戏，学会把那段历史的某些部分主题化。

en: Finally, the guild understandably reflects the social and political divisions of American society. Yet, by virtue of its professional claims, the guild cannot express political opinions as such—quite contrary, of course, to activists and lobbyists. Thus, ironically, the more important an issue for specific segments of civil society, the more subdued the interpretations of the facts offered by most professional historians. To a majority of the individuals involved in the controversies surrounding the Columbian quincentennial, the "Last Fact" exhibit at the Smithsonian on the

and Hiroshima, the excavation of slave cemeteries, or the building of the Vietnam Memorial, the statements produced by most historians seemed often bland or irrelevant. In these cases, as in many others, those to whom history mattered most looked for historical interpretations on the fringes of academia when not altogether outside it.
zh: 最后，行会可以理解地反映了美国社会的社会与政治分裂。然而，凭借其职业主张，行会不能直接表达政治意见——当然，这与活动家和游说者截然相反。于是，讽刺的是，一个问题对公民社会的特定部分越重要，大多数职业历史学家提供的事实解释就越低调。对卷入哥伦布五百周年、史密森学会关于“艾诺拉·盖伊”号与广岛的“最后的事实”展览、奴隶墓地发掘或越战纪念碑建造等争议的大多数人来说，大多数历史学家生产的声明常常显得平淡或不相关。在这些例子和许多其他例子中，历史对之最要紧的人，到学院边缘——如果不是完全到学院之外——去寻找历史解释。
body.review: 底本作 Last Fact。史密森学会档案所载拟展名称是 The Last Act: The Atomic Bomb and the End of World War II（《最后一幕：原子弹与第二次世界大战的结束》）。

en: Yet the fact that history is also produced outside of academia has largely been ignored in theories of history. Beyond a broad—and relatively recent—agreement on the situatedness of the professional historian, there is little concrete exploration of activities that occur elsewhere but impact significantly on the object of study. To be sure, such an impact does not lend itself easily to general formulas, a predicament that rebukes most theorists. I have noted that while most theorists acknowledge at the outset that history involves both the social process and narratives about that process, theories of history actually privilege one side as if the other did not matter.
zh: 然而，历史也在学院之外生产这一事实，在历史理论中大多被忽视。除了对职业历史学家的处境性达成一种宽泛——而且相对晚近——的共识之外，对于发生在别处、却显著影响研究对象的活动，几乎没有具体的探究。诚然，这种影响不容易套入通用公式，这个困境让大多数理论家却步。我已经指出：尽管大多数理论家一开始就承认历史既涉及社会过程、也涉及关于那个过程的叙述，历史理论实际上却偏袒一边，仿佛另一边无关紧要。

en: This one-sidedness is possible because theories of history rarely examine in detail the concrete production of specific narratives. Narratives are occasionally evoked as illustrations or, at best, deciphered as texts, but the process of their production rarely constitutes the object of study.

Similarly, most scholars would readily admit that historical production occurs in many sites. But the relative weight of these sites varies with context and these variations impose on the theorist the burden of the concrete. Thus, an examination of French palaces as sites of historical production can provide illustrative lessons for an understanding of Hollywood's role in U.S. historical consciousness, but no abstract theory can set,
, the rules that govern the relative impact of French castles and of U.S. movies on the academic history produced in these two countries.
zh: 这种片面性之所以可能，是因为历史理论很少详细考察具体叙述的具体生产。叙述偶尔被引来作为例证，或者至多被当作文本来解读，但它们的生产过程很少成为研究对象。
同样，大多数学者会欣然承认历史生产发生在许多场所。但这些场所的相对分量随语境变化，这些变化把具体性的重担压给理论家。因此，考察法国宫殿作为历史生产场所，可以为理解好莱坞在美国历史意识中的角色提供示例性的教训；但没有任何抽象理论能先验地设定规则，支配法国城堡和美国电影对这两国所生产学院史学的相对影响。

en: The heavier the burden of the concrete, the more likely it is to be bypassed by theory. Thus even the best treatments of academic history proceed as if what happened in the other sites was largely inconsequential. Yet is it really inconsequential that the history of America is being written in the same world where few little boys want to be Indians?
zh: 具体性的担子越重，就越可能被理论绕过。于是，就连对学院史学最好的处理，也仿佛其他场所发生的事大体无关紧要似的推进。可是，美国的历史正在同一个世界里被书写，而那个世界里几乎没有小男孩想当印第安人——这真的无关紧要吗？

en: Theorizing Ambiguity and Tracking Power
zh: 理论化歧义与追踪权力

en: History is always produced in a specific historical context. Historical actors are also narrators, and vice versa.
zh: 历史总是在特定的历史语境中被生产出来的。历史的行动者同时也是叙述者，反之亦然。

en: The affirmation that narratives are always produced in history leads me to propose two choices. First, I contend that a theory of the historical narrative must acknowledge both the distinction and the overlap between process and narrative. Thus, although this book is primarily about history as knowledge and narrative,
it fully embraces the ambiguity inherent in the two sides of historicity.
zh: 叙述总是在历史中被生产出来的——这一断言促使我提出两个选择。第一，我主张，一种关于历史叙述的理论必须同时承认过程与叙述之间的区分和重叠。因此，尽管本书主要讨论作为知识与叙述的历史，
它仍充分拥抱历史性两面所固有的歧义。

en: History, as social process, involves peoples in three distinct capacities: 1) as
, or occupants of structural positions; 2) as
in constant interface with a context; and 3) as

, that is, as voices aware of their vocality. Classical examples of what I call agents are the strata and sets to which people belong, such as class and status, or the roles associated with these. Workers, slaves, mothers are agents.
An analysis of slavery can explore the sociocultural, political, economic, and ideological structures that define such positions as slaves and masters.
zh: 历史作为社会过程，使人们以三种不同的身份参与其中：1）作为能动者，即结构位置的占据者；2）作为不断同所处情境相互作用的行动者；3）作为主体，也就是意识到自身发声能力的声音。我所谓能动者的经典例子，是人们所属的阶层与群体，如阶级和地位，以及与这些位置相关的角色。工人、奴隶、母亲都是能动者。
对奴隶制的分析可以探究那些界定奴隶与主人这类位置的社会文化、政治、经济和意识形态结构。

en: By actors, I mean the bundle of capacities that are specific in time and space in ways that both their existence and their understanding rest fundamentally on historical particulars. A comparison of African-American slavery in Brazil and the United States that goes beyond a statistical table must deal with the historical particulars that define the situations being compared. Historical narratives address particular situations and, in that sense, they must deal with human beings as actors.
zh: 我所说的行动者，指的是一组特定时空中的能力，其存在以及我们对它们的理解，从根本上都取决于具体的历史情境。对巴西和美国的非洲裔奴隶制所作的比较，若要超出一张统计表，就必须处理那些界定被比较情境的历史细节。历史叙述针对的是特定情境，在这个意义上，它必须把人类当作行动者来处理。

en: But peoples are also the subjects of history the way workers are subjects of a strike: they define the very terms under which some situations can be described. Consider a strike as a historical event from a strictly narrative viewpoint, that is, without the interventions that we usually put under such labels as interpretation or explanation. There is no way we can describe a strike without making the subjective capacities of the workers a central part of the description.

Stating their absence from the workplace is certainly not enough. We need to state that they collectively reached the decision to stay at home on what was supposed to be a regular working day. We need to add that they collectively acted upon that decision. But even such a description, which takes into account the workers’ position as actors, is not a competent description of a strike. Indeed, there are a few other contexts in which such a description could account for something else. Workers could have decided: if the snowfall exceeds ten inches tonight, none of us will come to work tomorrow. If we accept scenarios of manipulation or errors of interpretation among the actors, the possibilities become limitless. Thus, beyond dealing with the workers as actors, a competent narrative of a strike needs to claim access to the workers as purposeful subjects aware of their own voices. It needs their voice(s) in the first person or, at least, it needs to paraphrase that first person. The narrative must give us a hint of both the reasons why the workers refuse to work and the objective they think they are pursuing—even if that objective is limited to the voicing of protest. To put it most simply, a strike is a strike only if the workers think that they are striking. Their subjectivity is an integral part of the event and of any satisfactory description of that event.
zh: 但人们也是历史的主体，正如工人是罢工的主体：有些情境须用什么说法来描述，正是由他们决定的。不妨从纯粹叙述的观点——也就是排除我们通常归在解释或说明这类标签之下的那些介入——把罢工看作一个历史事件。我们无论如何描述一场罢工，都不可能不把工人作为主体的能力作为描述的核心部分。

仅仅陈述他们没有出现在工作场所，显然不够。我们需要陈述：他们集体作出决定，在本应是正常工作日的那天待在家里。我们还需要补充：他们集体依照那个决定行动了。但即便这样一种考虑了工人作为行动者之位置的描述，也不是对罢工的合格描述。的确，还有另外一些语境，同样的描述在其中可以说明别的事情。工人们可能决定的是：如果今晚降雪超过十英寸，明天我们谁也不来上班。如果我们接受行动者中间存在操纵或解释错误的情形，可能性就变得无穷无尽。因此，除了把工人当作行动者来处理，一部合格的罢工叙述还需要宣称能够触及作为有目的的主体、意识到自身声音的工人。它需要他们以第一人称发出的声音，或者至少需要对那个第一人称的转述。叙述必须让我们略微看到工人拒绝劳动的理由，以及他们自认为在追求的目标——哪怕那个目标仅限于发出抗议之声。说得最简单些：只有当工人认为自己在罢工时，罢工才是罢工。他们的主体性是该事件以及对该事件的任何令人满意的描述的内在组成部分。

en: Workers work much more often than they strike, but the capacity to strike is never fully removed from the condition of workers. In other words, peoples are not always subjects constantly confronting history as some academics would wish, but the capacity upon which they act to become subjects is always part of their condition. This subjective capacity ensures confusion because it makes human beings doubly historical or, more properly, fully historical. It engages them simultaneously in the sociohistorical process and in narrative constructions about that process. The embracing of this ambiguity, which is inherent in what I call the two sides of historicity, is the first choice of this book.
zh: 工人劳动的时候远多于罢工的时候，但罢工的能力从未完全从工人的处境中移除。换句话说，人们并不像某些学院人士所希望的那样，总是不断直面历史的主体，但他们赖以行动、成为主体的那种能力，始终是其处境的一部分。这种成为主体的能力注定带来混淆，因为它使人类双重地成为历史的，或者更准确地说，完全地成为历史的。它使人们同时投身于社会历史过程和关于那个过程的叙述建构。拥抱这种歧义——它内在于我所谓的历史性两面——是本书的第一个选择。

en: The second choice of this book is a concrete focus on the process of historical production rather than an abstract concern for the nature of history. The search for the nature of history has led us to deny ambiguity and either to demarcate precisely and at all times the dividing line between historical process and historical knowledge or to conflate at all times historical process and historical narrative. Thus between the mechanically “realist” and naively “constructivist” extremes, there is the more serious task of determining not what history is—a hopeless goal if phrased in essentialist terms—but how history works. For what history is changes with time and place or, better said, history reveals itself only through the production of specific narratives. What matters most are the process and conditions of production of such narratives. Only a focus on that process can uncover the ways in which the two sides of historicity intertwine in a particular context. Only through that overlap can we discover the differential exercise of power that makes some narratives possible and silences others.
zh: 本书的第二个选择，是具体地聚焦于历史的生产过程，而不是抽象地关切历史的本质。对历史本质的探求使我们否认歧义，要么在任何时候都精确划定历史过程与历史知识之间的分界线，要么在任何时候都把历史过程与历史叙述混为一谈。因此，在机械的“实在论”与天真的“建构主义”两个极端之间，还有一项更严肃的任务：不是确定历史是什么——若以本质主义的方式提问，这是个无望的目标——而是确定历史如何运作。因为历史是什么随时间和地点而变化，或者更准确地说，历史只有通过特定叙述的生产才显现自身。最重要的，是这类叙述的生产过程与生产条件。只有聚焦于那个过程，才能揭示历史性两面在特定语境中相互交织的方式。只有透过那种重叠，我们才能发现那种差别化的权力运作：它使某些叙述成为可能，并使另一些沉默。

en: Tracking power requires a richer view of historical production than most theorists acknowledge. We cannot exclude in advance any of the actors who participate in the production of history or any of the sites where that production may occur. Next to professional historians we discover artisans of different kinds, unpaid or unrecognized field laborers who augment, deflect, or reorganize the work of the professionals as politicians, students, fiction writers, filmmakers, and participating members of the public. In so doing, we gain a more complex view of academic history itself, since we do not consider professional historians the sole participants in its production.
zh: 追踪权力，需要一种比大多数理论家所承认的更丰富的历史生产观。我们不能预先排除任何参与历史生产的行动者，也不能预先排除这种生产可能发生的任何场所。在职业历史学家身旁，我们发现各式各样的匠人，发现在历史生产的各个场所劳动、却拿不到报酬或得不到承认的人——政客、学生、小说家、电影人以及参与其中的公众成员，他们扩充、偏转或重组专业人士的工作。这样一来，我们对学院史学本身也获得更复杂的看法，因为我们不再把职业历史学家视为其生产的唯一参与者。

en: This more comprehensive view expands the chronological boundaries of the production process. We can see that process as both starting earlier and going on later than most theorists admit. The process does not stop with the last sentence of a professional historian since the public is quite likely to contribute to history if only by adding its own readings to—and about—the scholarly productions. More important, perhaps, since the overlap between history as social process and history as knowledge is fluid, participants in any event may enter into the production of a narrative about that event before the historian as such reaches the scene. In fact, the historical narrative within which an actual event fits could precede that event itself, at least in theory, but perhaps also in practice. Marshall Sahlins suggests that the Hawaiians read their encounter with Captain Cook as the chronicle of a death foretold. But such exercises are not limited to the peoples without historians. How much do narratives of the end of the Cold War fit into a prepackaged history of capitalism in knightly armor? William Lewis suggests that one of Ronald Reagan’s political strengths was his capacity to inscribe his presidency into a prepackaged narrative about the United States. And an overall sketch of world historical production through time suggests that professional historians alone do not set the narrative framework into which their stories fit. Most often, someone else has already entered the scene and set the cycle of silences.
zh: 这种更全面的看法扩展了生产过程的时间边界。我们可以看到，那个过程的开始比大多数理论家承认的更早，延续也比他们承认的更晚。过程并不止于职业历史学家的最后一句话，因为公众很可能为历史作出贡献，哪怕只是用自己的解读补充学术成果，并对这些成果本身作出解读。也许更重要的是，既然作为社会过程的历史与作为知识的历史之间的重叠是流动的，任何事件的参与者都可能在历史学家本人到场之前，就进入关于那个事件的叙述的生产。事实上，一个实际事件所嵌入的历史叙述，可能先于那个事件本身，至少在理论上如此，也许在实践中亦然。马歇尔·萨林斯提出，夏威夷人把他们与库克船长的相遇读作一桩事先张扬的死亡纪事。但这类做法并不限于没有历史学家的民族。关于冷战终结的叙述，在多大程度上嵌入了一个预先包装好的、披着骑士铠甲的资本主义史？威廉·刘易斯提出，罗纳德·里根的政治长处之一，是他有能力把自己的总统任期铭写进一个预先包装好的关于美国的叙述。而对世界历史生产随时间演变的总体勾勒表明，并非只有职业历史学家在设定他们的故事所嵌入的叙述框架。大多数时候，已经有别人先入了场，设定了沉默的循环。

en: Does this expanded view still allow pertinent generalizations about the production of the historical narrative? The answer to this question is an unqualified yes, if we agree that such generalizations enhance our understanding of specific practices but do not provide blueprints that practice will supposedly follow or illustrate.
zh: 这种扩展了的看法，还允许对历史叙述的生产作出切题的概括吗？对这个问题的回答是无条件的肯定——只要我们同意，这类概括增进我们对具体实践的理解，却不提供实践据称会遵循或例证的蓝图。

en: Silences enter the process of historical production at four crucial moments: the moment of fact creation (the making of
); the moment of fact assembly (the making of

); and the moment of retrospective significance (the making of
in the final instance).
zh: 沉默在四个关键时刻进入历史的生产过程：事实创造的时刻（
的形成）；事实集结的时刻（
的形成）；事实提取的时刻（
的形成）；以及回溯赋予意义的时刻（归根结底，
的形成）。

en: These moments are conceptual tools, second-level abstractions of processes that feed on each other. As such, they are not meant to provide a realistic description of the making of any individual narrative. Rather, they help us understand why not all silences are equal and why they cannot be addressed—or redressed—in the same manner. To put it differently, any historical narrative is a particular bundle of silences, the result of a unique process, and the operation required to deconstruct these silences will vary accordingly.
zh: 这些时刻是概念工具，是对彼此推动的过程所作的二阶抽象。因此，它们并不打算对任何单个叙述的制造提供写实的描述。毋宁说，它们帮助我们理解：为什么并非所有沉默都平等，为什么它们不能以同一种方式被应对——或被补救。换句话说，任何历史叙述都是一束特定的沉默，是一个独特过程的结果，而解构这些沉默所需的操作也将随之变化。

en: The strategies deployed in this book reflect these variations. Each of the narratives treated in the next three chapters combines diverse types of silences. In each case, these silences crisscross or accumulate over time to produce a unique mixture. In each case I use a different approach to reveal the conventions and the tensions within that mixture.
zh: 本书采用的策略反映了这些差异。接下来三章处理的每一个叙述，都组合着不同类型的沉默。在每一个案例中，这些沉默随时间交错或累积，产生独特的混合物。在每一个案例中，我都用不同的进路来揭示那种混合物内部的惯例与张力。

en: In chapter 2, I sketch the image of a former slave turned colonel, now a forgotten figure of the Haitian Revolution. The evidence required to tell his story was available in the corpus I studied, in spite of the poverty of the sources. I only reposition that evidence to generate a new narrative. My alternative narrative, as it develops, reveals the silences that buried, until now, the story of the colonel.
zh: 在第二章，我勾勒一个由前奴隶成为上校的人的形象，他如今是海地革命中被遗忘的人物。尽管史料贫乏，讲述他的故事所需的证据在我研究的那批文献里已经存在。我只是重新安置那些证据，以生成一个新的叙述。我的替代性叙述在展开过程中，揭示出直到现在还把上校的故事埋没的种种沉默。

en: The general silencing of the Haitian Revolution by Western historiography is the subject of chapter 3. That silencing also is due to uneven power in the production of sources, archives, and narratives. But if I am correct that this revolution was unthinkable as it happened, the insignificance of the story is already inscribed in the sources, regardless of what else they reveal. There are no new facts here; not even neglected ones. Here, I have to make the silences speak for themselves. I do so by juxtaposing the climate of the times, the writings of historians on the revolution itself, and narratives of world history where the effectiveness of the original silence becomes fully visible.
zh: 西方史学对海地革命的普遍沉默化，是第三章的主题。那种沉默化同样源于史料、档案和叙述生产中的不均权力。但是，如果我说这场革命在发生之时是无法构想的这一点是对的，那么无论史料还揭示了别的什么，这个故事的无足轻重都已经铭写在史料之中。这里没有新事实，连被忽视的事实也没有。在这里，我必须让沉默自己说话。我的做法是并置时代氛围、历史学家关于革命本身的著述，以及那些让原初沉默的效力充分显现的世界历史叙述。

en: The discovery of America, the theme of chapter 4, provided me with yet another combination, thus compelling yet a third strategy. Here was an abundance of both sources and narratives. Until 1992, there was even a sense—although forged and recent—of global agreement on the significance of Columbus’s first trip. The main tenets of historical writings were inflected and bolstered through public celebrations that seemed to reinforce this significance. Within this wide-open corpus, silences are produced not so much by an absence of facts or interpretations as through conflicting appropriations of Columbus’s persona. Here, I do not suggest a new reading of the same story, as I do in chapter 2, or even alternative interpretations, as in chapter 3. Rather, I show how the alleged agreement about Columbus actually masks a history of conflicts. The methodological exercise culminates in a narrative about the competing appropriations of the discovery. Silences appear in the interstices of the conflicts between previous interpreters.
zh: 美洲的发现是第四章的主题，它给我提供了又一种组合，从而迫使我又采取第三种策略。这里史料和叙述都很丰富。直到1992年，甚至还存在一种——尽管是人为制造且晚近的——关于哥伦布首次航行意义的全球共识感。历史著述的主要信条，通过似乎强化了这一意义的公共庆典而被变奏和支撑。在这批可广泛取用的材料中，沉默的产生，与其说是因为事实或解释的缺席，不如说是因为对哥伦布其人的相互冲突的占用。在这里，我不像第二章那样提出对同一个故事的新解读，也不像第三章那样提出替代性解释。毋宁说，我展示关于哥伦布的所谓共识实际上如何掩盖着一部冲突史。这一方法论演练最终落实为一部关于对“发现”的竞争性占用的叙述。沉默出现在先前解释者之间冲突的缝隙里。

en: The production of a historical narrative cannot be studied, therefore, through a mere chronology of its silences. The moments I distinguish here overlap in real time. As heuristic devices, they only crystallize aspects of historical production that best expose when and where power gets into the story.
zh: 因此，对历史叙述的生产的研究，不能只是把其中的沉默排成一部编年史。我在这里区分的诸时刻在真实时间中相互重叠。作为启发性工具，它们只是使历史生产中的某些方面凸显出来，便于看清权力何时何地进入故事。

en: But even this phrasing is misleading if it suggests that power exists outside the story and can therefore be blocked or excised. Power is constitutive of the story. Tracking power through various “moments” simply helps emphasize the fundamentally processual character of historical production, to insist that what history is matters less than how history works; that power itself works together with history; and that the historians’ claimed political preferences have little influence on most of the actual practices of power. A warning from Foucault is helpful: “I don’t believe that the question of ‘who exercises power?’ can be resolved unless that other question ‘
’ is resolved at the same time.”
zh: 但即便这种措辞，如果它暗示权力存在于故事之外、因而可以被阻挡或切除，也仍是误导性的。权力是故事的构成性要素。透过各个“时刻”追踪权力，只是有助于强调历史生产根本上的过程性，坚持主张：比起历史是什么，历史如何运作更要紧；权力本身与历史一起运作；历史学家宣称的政治偏好对权力的大多数实际运作影响甚微。福柯的一个警告很有帮助：“我不相信‘谁行使权力？’这个问题能够得到解决，除非另一个问题‘
’同时得到解决。”

en: Power does not enter the story once and for all, but at different times and from different angles. It precedes the narrative proper, contributes to its creation and to its interpretation. Thus, it remains pertinent even if we can imagine a totally scientific history, even if we relegate the historians’ preferences and stakes to a separate, post-descriptive phase. In history, power begins at the source.
zh: 权力并非一劳永逸地进入故事，而是在不同的时间、从不同的角度进入。它先于叙述本身，参与叙述的创造和解释。因此，即便我们能想象一种完全科学的历史，即便我们把历史学家的偏好与利害归入一个独立的、后于描述的阶段，权力依然切题。在历史中，权力始于史料。

en: The play of power in the production of alternative narratives begins with the joint creation of facts and sources for at least two reasons. First, facts are never meaningless: indeed, they become facts only because they matter in some sense, however minimal. Second, facts are not created equal: the production of traces is always also the creation of silences. Some occurrences are noted from the start; others are not. Some are engraved in individual or collective bodies; others are not. Some leave physical markers; others do not. What happened leaves traces, some of which are quite concrete—buildings, dead bodies, censuses, monuments, diaries, political boundaries—that limit the range and significance of any historical narrative. This is one of many reasons why not any fiction can pass for history: the materiality of the sociohistorical process (historicity 1) sets the stage for future historical narratives (historicity 2).
zh: 替代性叙述生产中的权力运作，始于事实与史料的共同创造，理由至少有两个。第一，事实从不无意义：的确，它们之所以成为事实，恰恰因为它们在某种意义上要紧，哪怕这种意义微乎其微。第二，事实并非生而平等：痕迹的生产始终同时也是沉默的创造。有些事件从一开始就被记录；另一些则没有。有些铭刻在个体或集体的身体上；另一些则没有。有些留下物质标记；另一些则没有。发生过的事情留下痕迹，其中一些相当具体——建筑、尸体、人口普查、纪念碑、日记、政治边界——它们限定着任何历史叙述的范围与意义。这是并非任何虚构都能冒充历史的众多理由之一：社会历史过程的物质性（历史性1）为未来的历史叙述（历史性2）搭建了舞台。

en: The materiality of this first moment is so obvious that some of us take it for granted. It does not imply that facts are meaningless objects waiting to be discovered under some timeless seal but rather, more modestly, that history begins with bodies and artifacts: living brains, fossils, texts, buildings.
zh: 这第一个时刻的物质性如此显而易见，以至于我们中有些人视之为理所当然。它并不意味着事实是封存在某种超时间封印之下、等待被发现的无意义对象，它只表明：历史始于身体与器物：活的大脑、化石、文本、建筑。

en: The bigger the material mass, the more easily it entraps us: mass graves and pyramids bring history closer while they make us feel small. A castle, a fort, a battlefield, a church, all these things bigger than we that we infuse with the reality of past lives, seem to speak of an immensity of which we know little except that we are part of it. Too solid to be unmarked, too conspicuous to be candid, they embody the ambiguities of history. They give us the power to touch it, but not that to hold it firmly in our hands—hence the mystery of their battered walls. We suspect that their concreteness hides secrets so deep that no revelation may fully dissipate their silences. We imagine the lives under the mortar, but how do we recognize the end of a bottomless silence?
zh: 物质体量越大，就越容易把我们困住：万人坑与金字塔把历史拉近，同时让我们自觉渺小。一座城堡、一处要塞、一片战场、一座教堂，所有这些比我们更大、被我们注入往昔生活之实在性的东西，似乎都在诉说一种浩瀚，我们对它所知甚少，只知道自己身处其中。它们太坚固，不可能不留痕迹；太显眼，不可能坦白无隐——它们体现着历史的种种歧义。它们给我们触摸历史的权力，却不给我们把它牢牢握在手中的权力——它们那饱经摧残的墙壁的神秘由此而来。我们疑心，它们的具体性掩藏着如此深的秘密，以至于任何启示都无法完全驱散它们的沉默。我们想象灰泥之下那些人的生平，可是，我们如何辨认一场无底沉默的终结？

en: In fact, each narrative must renew this claim twice. From the viewpoint of its immediate producer(s), the narrative makes a claim to knowledge: that which is said to have happened is said to be known to have happened. Every historian delivers a narrative with a certificate of authenticity, however qualified. From the viewpoint of its audience, the historical narrative must pass a test of acceptance, which reinforces the claim to knowledge: that which is said to have happened is believed to have happened.

The differences between these rebuttals offer lessons in historical strategies. Pressac’s book faces head-on the revisionist’s challenge to treat the Holocaust as any other historical controversy and to deal with the facts and just the facts. It is the most “academic” in an old-fashioned way. Almost three-hundred footnotes of archival references, numerous pictures, graphs, and tables document the massive death machinery set up by the Nazis. Lipstadt takes the position that there should be no debate on “facts,” because such debate legitimizes revisionism; but she engages the revisionists polemically on their political motivations, which seems to me no less legitimizing and requires numerous allusions to empirical controversies. Vidal-Naquet consciously rejects the proposition that debates on “facts” and ideology are mutually exclusive. Although he avoids name-calling, he continuously expresses his moral outrage not only at the revisionist narrative but at the Holocaust. There would be no revisionism if there was no Holocaust. This strategy leaves him room for both a methodological and political critique of revisionism, and for empirical challenge on the “facts” he chooses to debate. Vidal-Naquet also avoids the trap of Jewish exceptionalism, which could easily lead to a view of history as revenge and justify use and misuse of the Holocaust narrative: Auschwitz cannot explain Chabra and Chatila.

这些反驳之间的差异提供了历史策略上的教益。普雷萨克的书正面迎击修正主义者的挑战——把大屠杀当作任何其他历史争论来处理，只处理事实，而且只处理事实。它以老派的方式最为“学术”。近三百条档案出处的脚注、大量图片、图表与表格，记录了纳粹建立的大规模死亡机器。利普斯塔特采取这样的立场：不应就“事实”展开辩论，因为这种辩论会使修正主义合法化；但她以论战方式追究修正主义者的政治动机，在我看来这同样是在使其合法化，而且需要大量提及经验层面的争论。维达尔-纳凯自觉地拒绝“事实”辩论与意识形态辩论互斥的命题。他虽然避免辱骂，却不断表达道德义愤——不仅针对修正主义叙述，也针对大屠杀本身。没有大屠杀，就不会有修正主义。这一策略使他既能在方法论与政治层面批判修正主义，又能就他选择辩论的“事实”提出经验层面的质疑。维达尔-纳凯还避免了犹太例外论的陷阱——那种例外论很容易把历史变成复仇，并为大屠杀叙述的使用与滥用辩护：奥斯维辛解释不了沙布拉和沙蒂拉。
